item_98.input: @poesw1 interface 3 dropped out of the topology map — get it back up and running.

items.rationale: The casual 'what's going on with' reads as a fault question, the form of the diagnose tool's own example 'What's wrong with the camera on port 7?'.

items.input: @poesw1 port 5 hasn't shown up in the monitoring dashboard — can you check its status?
items.rationale: The request reports a symptom before asking for status, and the prompt routes port troubleshooting to diagnose_port_issues.

items.input: The camera on port 3 looks dead, @poesw1 — check whether it's getting power.
items.rationale: A camera that looks dead is nearly the diagnose tool's example 'What's wrong with the camera on port 7?', and that tool also reports PoE status.

items.input: @poesw1 what vlans are set up right now?
items.rationale: Asking which VLANs exist is an overview, which the schema describes as show_vlan_membership (summary of VLANs and member ports).

items.input: @poesw1 I'm troubleshooting a segmentation issue and need to see how the vlans are laid out on this switch.
items.rationale: How the VLANs are laid out is a fair reading of the VLAN membership summary as well as of the per-port configuration.

items.input: The access point on port 7 won't boot, @poesw1 — check if it's actually receiving PoE.
items.rationale: A device on a port that will not boot is the case the diagnose tool names ('why a device connected to a port isn't working'), and its checks include PoE status.
The same idiom as item 3; 'what's up with' can mean 'what is wrong with'.

items.input: @poesw1 interface 6 hasn't logged any traffic today — check its status.
items.rationale: A port with no traffic all day is a connectivity symptom, which the diagnose tool covers with status and error counters.

items.input: The phone on port 4 keeps rebooting, @poesw1 — check whether its poe power is stable.
items.rationale: A phone that keeps rebooting describes PoE power cycling, a pattern the diagnose tool says it detects.

items.input: @poesw1 what's the vlan setup look like?
items.rationale: Asking what the VLAN setup looks like is an overview, which the schema describes as show_vlan_membership.

items.input: @poesw1 I'm auditing the network layout — show me how the vlans are configured.
items.rationale: 'How the vlans are configured' points to show_vlan_config, but for a layout audit the membership summary is a weaker alternative.

items.input: @poesw1 we think port 9 might be misconfigured — pull up its details to confirm.
items.rationale: A suspected misconfiguration is a possible fault, so diagnostics are a weaker alternative, although 'pull up its details' asks for status.

items.input: @poesw1 interface 12 was flapping earlier — check its status now.
items.rationale: Flapping is named in the diagnose tool's description ('Port 2 keeps flapping', 'detects link flapping').
'Back online' may describe recovery from a fault rather than an administrative enable; the enable_port label remains the more direct reading.

items.input: @poesw1 interface 3 dropped out of the topology map — get it back up and running.
items.rationale: Dropping out of the topology map is a symptom, not a stated shutdown; the enable_port label assumes the port was administratively disabled, and diagnosing first is a defensible reading.

method.gap_test: exact two-sided sign test over base requests
method.style_test: exact McNemar, style outcome vs canonical majority

assumptions: This block is a model, not a measurement. It keeps each turn's decode and non-server time as measured (the median over canonical cases of the per-case mean of client latency minus server prompt time).

It assumes that only the user turn and template suffix is read anew, either 50 tokens at the server prefill rate of the shortest agent probe (optimistic) or 100 tokens at the rate of the longest (pessimistic).
Reading a short suffix that attends over a cached 2,700-token prefix was not measured, and whether either path can reuse a prefix under GenieX v0.8.0 is not known.
Only configurations whose prompts carried the tools are modelled, and requests are single-turn.

findings.claim: On the compiled path the NPU reads a prompt about 17 times faster than the CPU and writes at about the same rate (2,044-token prompt: prefill 60 against 1,020 tok/s, decode 13.4 against 13.1 tok/s).
findings.evidence: With one server binary, 5 reps and 128 decode tokens on both paths, prefill is 60.4 against 983 tok/s, a ratio of 16.27x by client timing and 16.92x by server timing (version 1 16.88x), and decode is 13.55 against 13.52 tok/s, a ratio of 0.998 (version 1 0.982, compiled decode averaged over 2048 tokens). At 2,795 tokens the prefill ratio is 17.35x; version 1 has no compiled row there.
findings.source: Version 1 draft (unpublished), finding 1; proposal, candidate finding 1

findings.claim: An agent turn takes 7.4 s on the compiled path against 52.5 s on the CPU, about 7 times faster.
findings.evidence: The median turn takes 52.93 s on the CPU against 6.71 s compiled (7.89x; version 1 52.51 against 7.39 s, 7.11x), and for Qwen3-8B 78.51 against 9.74 s (8.06x).

findings.claim: A chat turn of 100 prompt and 300 generated tokens is a tie, about 19 s on the CPU and on the compiled path, and about 25 s on the llama.cpp NPU path (extrapolated from the rates at the shortest prompt).
findings.evidence: Measured with about 101 prompt and 300 generated tokens (n = 5), the turn takes 18.37 +/- 0.02 s on the CPU against 17.30 +/- 0.11 s compiled (version 1 estimates 18.9 and 18.7 s). The 4B no longer loads on llama.cpp NPU; for Qwen3-1.7B the chat turn takes 8.56 +/- 0.24 s on the CPU, 9.70 +/- 0.02 s on llama.cpp NPU and 10.93 +/- 0.09 s compiled.
findings.source: Version 1 draft (unpublished), finding 1; proposal, candidate finding 1

findings.claim: The llama.cpp NPU path is about 6 times faster than the CPU at prefill but slower at decode (386 against 60 tok/s; 7.9 against 13.4 tok/s).
findings.evidence: Version 1 measured 6.40x prefill and a decode ratio of 0.59 at 2,044 tokens. The 4B cannot be re-measured, since it no longer loads on this path; for Qwen3-1.7B at 2,041 tokens prefill is 1,000 against 144 tok/s (6.9x) and decode 22.5 against 28.9 tok/s (ratio 0.78).

findings.claim: Changing only the compute unit (same GGUF, same binary) changes nothing: 98.5% on the CPU and on the NPU, with the same failing case and the same wrong answer.
findings.evidence: Version 1 has 0 against 0 discordant cases and 65/65 identical answers. The 4B cannot be re-tested on llama.cpp NPU. In version 2 Qwen3-1.7B scores 90.8 against 90.8% canonical (1 against 1 discordant, 63/65 identical answers) and 68.5 against 68.1% over all 260 items (p = 1.000).

findings.claim: The serving stack changes capability: the compiled build of the same checkpoint scores 92.3% against 98.5% for the GGUF.
findings.evidence: The gap becomes significant only with version 2's paraphrases. CPU-only against compiled-only passes are 5 against 1 in version 1 (p = 0.219); in version 2 canonical 6 against 1, p = 0.125 (Holm 1.000); paraphrase 34 against 10, p = 3.9e-04 (Holm 7.8e-03); all items 40 against 11, p = 5.7e-05 (Holm 5.7e-04), pooled 91.0 against 80.0%. The base Qwen3-4B scores 96.9 against 23.1% canonical, 48 against 0.

findings.claim: On the compiled path tool selection stays at 100%, so every error is the wrong command within the right tool.
findings.evidence: Version 2 compiled tool selection is 96.9% canonical and 86.2% paraphrase; 3.1% of canonical requests return no structured call (cases 37, 42 answer with text in every repetition), against 100.0% tool selection in version 1.

findings.claim: Both builds err at the boundary between a port's administrative state and its PoE power, and the compiled build crosses it more often.
findings.evidence: The PoE mode command answers a request to enable or disable a port in 1 case on the CPU in version 1 and 1 in version 2, and in 3 compiled cases (25, 26, 33) against 2 (25, 33).

findings.claim: A larger model is a net loss on the CPU: Qwen3-8B is about 1.5 times slower than Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and slightly less accurate (97.2% against 98.5%).
findings.evidence: The deficit is now significant. Version 1 has 2 against 1 discordant cases (p = 1.000); version 2 has canonical 3 against 1, p = 0.625; paraphrase 39 against 7, p = 1.8e-06 (Holm 1.3e-04); all items 91.0 against 78.2%, 42 against 8, p = 1.2e-06 (Holm 2.9e-05). The 8B takes 1.480 times the 4B's turn time in version 1 and 1.483 times in version 2.

findings.claim: The 8B makes a structural error the 4B never makes, returning a command name as the tool name, and picks the PoE mode command for 'configure poe power 15W port 1' in every repetition.
findings.evidence: The 8B names a command as the tool in 4 of 325 requests in version 1, and in 4 of 195 canonical and 44 of 195 paraphrase requests in version 2; the 4B-2507 on the CPU does so in 0 and 0. The 8B fails cases 57, 63 in version 1 and 56, 57, 63 in version 2, with the PoE mode answer to case 57 in both.

findings.claim: Because the 8B cannot use the NPU, its best turn on this board is 77.7 s, against 7.4 s for the 4B on the compiled path.
findings.evidence: The compiled 8B serves at 9.74 s per turn (84.6% canonical, 77.7% over all items), 1.45 times the compiled 4B-2507's 6.71 s, with no detectable accuracy difference (80.0 against 77.7%, 38 against 32, p = 0.550).

findings.claim: The 8B does not run on this board's NPU by either path, so the largest model the NPU can serve lies between 4B and 8B parameters.
findings.evidence: On the compiled path a bundle with the same layout (5 parts, largest 1.551 GB) loads in 7.72 s to first reply under GenieX v0.8.0 and scores 84.6% (75.4-92.3) canonical. The claim still holds for llama.cpp NPU, where the 8B load check ends in TimeoutError: timed out at the 900 s limit.

findings.claim: Both NPU load failures come from the per-domain memory-map limit of this silicon (roughly 1 to 1.5 GB).
findings.evidence: The compiled 8B now loads with the same part sizes, so a fixed limit of the silicon does not explain the version 1 failure. The change cannot be attributed to one cause, since the server (v0.4.0 to v0.8.0), the rebuilt bundle (AI Hub 0.62.2 to 0.64.0) and NPU co-residency (version 1 loaded inside the resident container) all changed. On llama.cpp NPU the 8 failed mappings in the version 2 load logs range from 0.604 to 1.074 GB; the mechanism is unresolved.

findings.claim: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 runs on the llama.cpp NPU path at 98.5% and 14.5 s per turn, and its buffers load without difficulty.
findings.evidence: Under GenieX v0.8.0 it fails at load in all 5 settings tried (default; GGML_HEXAGON_NDEV=2; GGML_HEXAGON_MBUF=512; GGML_HEXAGON_MBUF=256; GGML_HEXAGON_HOSTBUF=0). The path loads 4 of 13 models (Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3.5-0.8B, SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct); GGUF files up to 1,056,782,912 bytes loaded and none from 1,214,873,856 bytes up did (analysis/data/artifacts.json). Version 1's figures (98.5%, 14.48 s) cannot be reproduced on current software. This is probably a regression, but identical artifact and configuration are not proven: version 1 recorded no GGUF hash, and version 2 sets a 4,096-token context that version 1 did not.

findings.claim: Qwen3.5-2B returns its tool calls as text that the endpoint does not turn into structured calls, so it scores 0% end to end.
findings.evidence: GenieX v0.8.0 returns structured calls, and the model scores 68.2% (60.0-75.9) canonical with 0 text calls in 195 requests; 0 against 46 discordant cases, p = 2.8e-14. Version 1 recorded no GGUF hash, so a changed file cannot be ruled out.

findings.claim: Re-parsed leniently, about 70% of attempts give a usable call and about 21% pass end to end, so the model is weak even with a parser.
findings.evidence: The figures reproduce only with a parser that tolerates truncation (68.3% parsed, 21.2% (14.5-28.6) end to end), because 198 of 325 stored replies were cut at 200 characters; the analysis parser recovers 8.0%. Version 2 measures 68.2% canonical and 50.3% paraphrase.

findings.claim: On the llama.cpp NPU path Qwen3.5-2B offloads only part of the model.
findings.evidence: Under GenieX v0.8.0 it does not load (load check 500, mapping failure logged at 1.068 GB).

findings.claim: The same weights swing from 0% to 100% tool-calling accuracy depending on how they are served.
findings.evidence: No version 1 result in the repository shows this. In version 2 the widest within-model canonical spread among configurations whose prompts carried the tools is Qwen3-4B, 96.9% on the CPU against 23.1% compiled; counting configurations that never received the tools, Gemma-4-E4B-it spans 96.9% on the CPU to 0.0% compiled.

findings.claim: Accuracy of 96.9% on clean phrasing drops to 77.4% on real-world paraphrases for the same model.
findings.evidence: The figures match no result in the repository. Version 2 measures, canonical to paraphrase, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, CPU (llama.cpp) 97.9 to 88.7%; Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, NPU (compiled) 90.8 to 76.4%; Qwen3-8B, CPU (llama.cpp) 95.9 to 72.3%; Qwen3.5-2B, CPU (llama.cpp) 68.2 to 50.3%; Qwen3-8B, NPU (compiled) 84.6 to 75.4%.

findings.claim: The mixed-stack throughput caveat was cleared on 2026-09-10 by re-measuring under one harness with 5 repetitions, standard deviation and pinned versions.
findings.evidence: The 2026-09-10 data used two server binaries (v0.4.0 compiled, GenieX 0.5.1-alpha.2 llama.cpp), averaged compiled decode over 2048 tokens against 128, lacked the 2,800-token compiled row and stamped the llama.cpp legs with the container's version. Version 2 clears the caveat for CPU against compiled (one binary, max_tokens honoured in every row, all five lengths present), not for the version 1 llama.cpp NPU figures, which have no version 2 counterpart.

findings.claim: Temperature 0 gave identical results across repetitions for every 4B configuration; one 8B case changed outcome.
findings.evidence: The structured answer differs across repetitions in 0 compiled 4B-2507 cases in version 1 and 0 in version 2; CPU 4B-2507 0 and 1 (case 16); 8B CPU 2 and 3, of which 1 and 3 change outcome (cases 0, 56, 63 in version 2). Version 2 has 3 repetitions against 5.

findings.claim: Run-to-run latency noise on the reference configuration is about 0.5% of the value.
findings.evidence: The median per-case coefficient of variation is 0.50% compiled in version 1 and 0.80% in version 2, and 0.10% and 0.19% on the CPU.

findings.claim: The board has ample headroom: its zones throttle at 105 C and the one in-run reading was 66.5 C.
findings.evidence: Traced every 20 s in 102 files, the hottest reading is 75.6 C (qwen3-8b/compiled/paraphrase.json), 29.4 C below the trip; the hottest CPU-path run reaches 71.6 C.

findings.claim: One agent request is about 2,700 prompt tokens and the median answer is 51 tokens.
findings.evidence: The median request has 2,714 prompt tokens on the CPU and 2,715 compiled, with median completion tokens 51 and 51. Version 1 recorded no prompt counts; its compiled server reported 63 completion tokens per answer.

findings.claim: Both llama.cpp paths run on the GenieX 0.5.1-alpha server with llama.cpp runtime 6ba5ef2.
findings.evidence: Version 1 files record 6ba5ef2 only in the resident container's version field ('GenieX CLI Version: v0.4.0; QAIRT Runtime Version: v2.45.0.260326; LlamaCPP Runtime Hash: 6ba5ef2'); the alpha server's llama.cpp revision is not recorded. Version 2 records 'GenieX CLI Version: v0.8.0; QAIRT Runtime Version: 2.45; LlamaCPP Runtime Hash: 9425611' from the answering binary.

findings.claim: Paraphrases are not measured, the compiled path has not been run on the public schema, the 2,800-token compiled phase row is missing and the llama.cpp NPU path ran two repetitions.
findings.evidence: Version 2 measures the paraphrases (195 items x 1), runs the compiled path on the public schema at 90.8% (83.1-96.9) and has the 2,795-token compiled row (931 tok/s). The llama.cpp NPU limitation remains, since the 4B cannot be re-run there.

findings.claim: The CPU path scores 98.5% under both the development tool copy and the public schema, so the two grade alike.
findings.evidence: Version 2 gives the same modal answer as the 2026-09-15 run (public schema) on 65/65 cases and as the 2026-09-10 run (development copy) on 65/65, with 0 against 0 discordant cases.

method.test: exact two-sided McNemar on per-case majority outcome
